六级大纲词汇 · 10英文原文

A Vote for the Last Bus

给末班公交的一票 · 593 词 · 6 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1The incumbent mayor wanted to cancel a late bus to pay for a route to a new venue. He called the referendum a test of his electoral mandate. A civic coalition questioned the ballot. Maya, a hospital nurse, was a constituent from a district that used the last bus. A short transfer might preserve both routes. She asked the council to convene a hearing before it framed the choice as one district's victory over another. Several colleagues joined her in solidarity. They feared an escalation between districts, while the mayor had become preoccupied with the turnout of his own supporters.

2A college chancellor offered to dedicate a parking area for transfers and enlist volunteers. The transport bureaucracy would not release a schedule until it knew who would pay. A partisan group suspected patronage and threatened a boycott. A college affiliate would coordinate volunteers if the council could entrust the trial to an autonomous board. Party affiliation would not determine membership. To Maya's dismay, the deadlock turned optimism into skepticism. She asked an independent mediator to confer with each constituency. The college needed lighting, the council wanted steady turnout, and hospital staff needed a departure they could catch. The mediator wrote each request down.

3The first interim plan proposed a voucher. Eligibility depended on a worker's employer. Maya feared that rule would alienate cleaners who worked through agencies. She proposed an amendment covering every shift worker. A refugee center requested the same access for its residents, who relied on humanitarian support. A new route was imperative for workers who otherwise relied on the dole. The director wanted transitional fares that would foster access and safeguard existing routes. Through mediation they reached terms that the college and the center both endorsed.

4Before the trial could start, a bureaucrat found a problem with the transport appropriation. The designation of the grant barred spending on lighting. The mayor wanted to override it. An assertive councillor asked him to amend the grant and seek ratification. A skeptical member asked who would run the route if the college withdrew. Maya's coalition offered a fallback that required no unilateral commitment. The council agreed to appropriate funds for a trial. It would preside over a hearing before deciding whether to ratify the agreement.

5Student volunteers mobilized after a strike threatened the first departure. The trial still drew unprecedented turnout. By the second week two departures carried most passengers. The transport office kept those and removed one lightly used trip. The mayor's predecessor changed his stance after riding with a cleaner. To keep the disagreement from escalating, Maya asked the opposition to nominate someone to check the figures. The nomination went to a former opponent. The nominee had opposed the plan on the first ballot. His skeptical stance meant both sides trusted him to read the figures. His endorsement mattered because he backed the timetable with figures. His rhetorical restraint put a stop to the mayor's campaign rhetoric.

6The electorate voted to retain the service. An affirmative vote let the council enact the plan with a review date beyond the mayor's tenure. Its enactment kept enough local autonomy to adjust the schedule. The bureau vowed to abide by the new rules and published a transition date. The inauguration was a quiet one. Maya took the bus and watched a student help a nurse onto it. She had once thought a bold speech would settle the issue. What mattered was a small transfer that let the two routes share a stop. On the timetable it was a dot that could unify two schedules.

六级大纲词汇 · 10中文译文

给末班公交的一票

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1现任市长想取消一班夜间公交，把钱用来开一条通往新场馆的线路。他说，公投将检验选民是否还支持他的施政主张。一个市民联盟质疑选票上的选项。医院护士玛雅来自依赖末班车的选区。安排一次短途换乘，也许能把两条线都保住。她请议会先举行听证会，别把这件事说成一个区赢、另一个区输。几位同事来声援她。他们担心区与区之间的争执升级，市长却一直在意自己的支持者会来多少。

2一所大学的校长愿意留出一片停车区供换乘，还能招募志愿者。交通部门要先确定由谁付钱，才肯公布时刻表。一个党派团体怀疑其中有人情交易，扬言抵制。一名大学下属机构的成员提出，如果议会能把试运行交给独立委员会，他就负责协调志愿者。委员人选不按党派归属决定。僵局让玛雅很失望，先前的乐观变成了怀疑。她请独立调解人与各选区商谈。调解人记下了各方的需求，学校要照明，议会要稳定的客流，医院职工要赶得上最后一班车。

3临时方案先提出发乘车券，领取资格取决于雇主。玛雅怕通过中介受雇的清洁工会被排除在外，便提出修正，让所有轮班职工都能用。一个难民中心也为依靠人道援助的住户争取相同的乘车机会。对那些没工作就得靠救济的人来说，新线路很重要。中心主任希望有一个过渡票价，既让居民坐得起车，也保留原有线路。经调解，学校和中心都接受了条件。

4试运行前，一名行政人员发现交通拨款有个问题。补助款指定了用途，不能用于照明。市长想绕过规定。一名态度坚定的议员要求他修改拨款方案并寻求批准。一名心存疑虑的议员问，如果学校退出，谁来运营线路？玛雅所在的联盟提出一个备用办法，任何一方都不用单独作出承诺。议会同意拨款试运行，并将在主持一场听证会后决定是否批准长期协议。

5一场罢工差点使首班车无法开出，学生志愿者赶紧行动。第一晚乘车人数还是创下纪录。到第二周，大部分乘客集中在两个班次。交通部门保留它们，取消了一班客流少的车。市长的前任与一位清洁工同乘后改变了立场。为了避免争议升级，玛雅请反对方提名一人核查数字。被提名的人第一次投票时反对过这个方案。正因为他一直审慎，两方都信任他核对的数据。他能拿数字支持新时刻表，他的赞同才有分量。他讲话很克制，市长也收起了竞选式的说辞。

6选民投票决定保留服务。议会依法通过方案，把复审时间定在市长任期结束后，也给当地留出调整班次的自主权。交通部门承诺遵守新规，并公布了过渡日期。开通仪式很简单。玛雅坐上车，看见一个学生扶着护士上车。她原先以为一场有气势的演说就能解决争议，真正起作用的是让两条路线共用一站的换乘办法。在时刻表上，它只是一个小点，却把两套时间接到了一起。
